title: Sony Pictures TV Exec Mike Wald to Retire After 32 Years; Jason Spivak, Paul Littmann Named Presidents of Distribution & Networks (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Sony Pictures Television distribution and networks co-president Mike Wald is retiring after 32 years with the company, the studio was set to announc
body:
Sony Pictures Television distribution and networks co-president Mike Wald is retiring after 32 years with the company, the studio was set to announce Thursday morning. The news comes as Sony Pictures’ TV exec VP of North America Distribution Flory Bramnick also recently announced her departure. 

	“I have had the distinct privilege of working closely with Mike and Flory for many years, and it is hard to overstate the impact they have had on our business and the people around them,” Sony Pictures TV chairman Keith Le Goy said in a memo to staff. As part of the changeover, Le Goy also revealed a new structure for its distribution and networks unit.
	

	Among the changes: Jason Spivak and Paul Littmann have been named presidents of distribution and networks. Spivak was previously co-president of distribution and networks, while Littmann was most recently executive VP of global distribution for Sony Pictures TV. They’ll both report to Le Goy.


	“Jason and Paul know our business, our content and our partners incredibly well and they bring the experience, ambition and judgment to continue driving the organization forward,” Le Goy said in a memo to staff. “I am excited about what they will accomplish together.”

	Also, Mark Young will serve as head of international. He had already overseen EMEA (Europe, Middle East, Africa), he’ll now also include LATAM (Latin America) and APAC (Asia-Pacific). Young will report to Spivak and Littmann. And as Variety previously reported, Monica Veiga now oversees North America as exec VP of distribution, North America, with Bramnick’s exit.
	

	With the changes, Sony Pictures TV is also expanding its interest in distribution for YouTube, FAST channels, digital platforms and other platforms. The studio will hire a leader to oversee its YouTube and digital platforms business, reporting to Spivak and Littmann. 

	“We have strong momentum across the business, including in areas with significant potential for continued growth such as YouTube, FAST, digital platforms and other performance-based models,” LeGoy added in his memo. “Our independence gives us a unique advantage in pursuing these opportunities, with the flexibility to move quickly, work across virtually every major platform and market and continually find new ways to maximize the value and reach of our content.”

	As for Wald, the exec’s career included roles across the U.S., Asia and Europe. In Asia, he helped launch AXN Asia and SET India; later, he led distribution across Europe, the Middle East and Africa and then took on more global responsibilities.

	Here is Le Goy’s memo to staff:

	Team,

	I want to update you on some important changes within our Distribution & Networks organization.

	After 32 years with Sony Pictures Television, Mike Wald has decided to retire at the end of this year. It is with mixed emotions that I announce his decision, which follows the news we shared earlier this month that Flory Bramnick will be stepping away after 24 years with the company. I have had the distinct privilege of working closely with Mike and Flory for many years, and it is hard to overstate the impact they have had on our business and the people around them.

	Mike’s career at Sony has quite literally spanned the globe. He began in corporate development, working in both Culver City and Hong Kong during a period of significant growth across Asia’s entertainment markets. He helped cultivate some of our earliest relationships in the region and was part of the team that developed and launched AXN Asia and SET India. Mike later returned to Los Angeles as a key leader on our global pay television team before going on to lead our distribution business across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. He ultimately took on broader global leadership responsibilities, bringing a deep understanding of the marketplace, trusted relationships with partners and steady judgment that have been invaluable as our industry has transformed — all while never losing his unique sense of humor.
	

	Flory has also been instrumental in building and shaping our business in North America. Since joining Sony in strategic sales in 2002, she has consistently been ahead of where the marketplace is going — ultimately leading the distribution of our film and television content across platforms in the U.S. and Canada. Throughout it all, she has continually found new ways to expand the reach and value of our content and build strong, enduring partnerships with our key customers.

	Beyond their many accomplishments, Mike and Flory have been generous colleagues, trusted partners and mentors to so many people across Sony. They have helped develop the next generation of leaders, and their influence will be felt here for many years to come.

	While we are very sad to see them go, I am incredibly optimistic about what lies ahead for our Distribution & Networks business. We have tremendous depth and experience across our leadership team, and I’m delighted to announce that Jason Spivak and Paul Littmann will jointly lead the organization as Presidents of Distribution & Networks, reporting directly to me. Jason and Paul know our business, our content and our partners incredibly well and they bring the experience, ambition and judgment to continue driving the organization forward. I am excited about what they will accomplish together.

	Reporting to Jason and Paul, Mark Young will take on the role of EVP, Head of International, expanding his current oversight of EMEA to include LATAM and APAC, with the leadership in those regions reporting to him. Monica Veiga, EVP, TV Distribution, North America, will expand her responsibilities to include the broader North America business.

	We have strong momentum across the business, including in areas with significant potential for continued growth such as YouTube, FAST, digital platforms and other performance-based models. Our independence gives us a unique advantage in pursuing these opportunities, with the flexibility to move quickly, work across virtually every major platform and market and continually find new ways to maximize the value and reach of our content.

	We are exceptionally well positioned for continued success. We have extraordinary content, deep relationships across the marketplace and, most importantly, a remarkable team that knows how to turn those strengths into growth. Our business moves fast; we will move faster.
	

	Please join me in thanking Mike and Flory for their extraordinary contributions to Sony Pictures Television, and in congratulating Jason, Paul, Mark and Monica on their new roles.

	Keith

schema.headline: Sony Pictures TV Exec Mike Wald to Retire After 32 Years; Jason Spivak, Paul Littmann Named Presidents of Distribution & Networks (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon
description:
“Neagley” has been renewed for Season 2 at Amazon, Variety has learned. 

	The “Reacher” spinoff series originally debuted on Prime Video on Sept. 1
body:
“Neagley” has been renewed for Season 2 at Amazon, Variety has learned. 

	The “Reacher” spinoff series originally debuted on Prime Video on Sept. 16, the same day as the “Reacher” Season 4 finale. Per Amazon, the first season has reached 40 million viewers in its first 13 days of availability, though Amazon does not define how they calculate viewership. 

	The streamer added that “Neagley” Season 1 is the number four most-viewed original series debut in Prime Video history, and has achieved 52% of its viewership internationally.  
	

	News of the “Neagley” renewal comes just days after it was reported that “Reacher” had been renewed for Season 6 while Season 5 is still in production. 


	Maria Sten reprises the role of Frances Neagley in the spinoff series, with Neagley having been Jack Reacher’s protege in the Army and now working as a private investigator. The logline for the debut season states, “When [Neagley] learns that a beloved friend from her past has been killed in a suspicious accident, she becomes hell-bent on justice.” 

	“Audiences around the world have embraced Frances Neagley as a force all her own,” said Peter Friedlander, head of global television for Amazon MGM Studios. “Maria Sten delivers a commanding, layered performance that drives every episode, and Nick Santora and Nicholas Wootton have built a world that is both thrilling and compelling. We are excited to continue this story and explore what’s next for Neagley with our partners at Paramount Television Studios.”

	Along with Sten, the cast for Season 1 included Greyston Holt, Adeline Rudolph, Jasper Jones, Matthew Del Negro, and Damon Herriman. “Reacher” star Alan Ritchson appeared in a guest star role. 
	

	“Neagley” is based on the character first featured in Lee Child’s Jack Reacher novels. Nock Santora and Nicholas Wootton serve as writers, executive producers, and co-showrunners. Child also executive produces along with Don Granger, Sam Hill, Adam Higgs, and Lisa Kussner. Paramount Television Studios and Amazon MGM Studios produce. Carolyn Harris, Kenny Madrid, and Niko Fernandez oversee the project for Paramount Television Studios.

schema.headline: ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon

title: ‘The Influencer Project’ Review: Found Footage Terror Takes a Tepid Danish Holiday
description: An opening text announcing “This film is influenced by real events” provides the first and last moment of inspiration in “The Influencer Project,” w
body:
An opening text announcing “This film is influenced by real events” provides the first and last moment of inspiration in “The Influencer Project,” whether the joke is deliberate or not. Mike Nybroe’s debut feature is far from the first horror movie to posit practitioners of the titular digital-age profession as a killer’s prey, and surely won’t be the last. Billed as coming “from the creators of ‘The Blair Witch Project’” — and that film’s co-director Eduardo Sanchez is a producer here — it could be worse. Yet despite not strictly hewing to the found-footage template established by the 1999 sleeper hit, this opus lands smack in the mediocre middle of umpteen forgettable imitations churned out ever since.
	

	British aspiring singer turned social media personality Chiara King get an “introducing” credit playing herself in staged circumstances, terrorized by a stalker while on a promotional trip to Copenhagen. She, like the film, is competent without leaving much of an impression — neither a star nor a franchise is born here. Still, horror fans up for seeing anything new in the countdown to Halloween will find this new “Project” meets basic subgenre expectations, even if it does nothing to elevate or transcend them.


	A prologue finds a teenage girl (Ronja Hauge Schierup) announcing to livestream viewers that “Today is the day we are going to go viral.” She then performs a drastic act that guarantees only the saddest kind of fame. Selling herself as a contrastingly upbeat life-lover is twentysomething Chiara, whose own “viral kissing video” (which we don’t actually see) apparently kickstarted an online celebrity with 50 million views. That got her a manager, Alice (Jazmine Summer), along with lucrative product tie-in deals, and now an invitation to visit the Danish capital as part of a tourism campaign. In exchange, she’ll post her own typical videos while shopping, sightseeing, clubbing, sampling select restaurants, and so on. She’ll also have a local documentary crew filming her every move, its principal personnel cameraman Mike (played by director Nybroe) and younger assistant Victor (Luca Storm).
	

	All this is innocuous enough, Chiara included. Alice tells her, “Your followers love you being you.” But in a dramatic context, her persona as a nice, pretty but relatably ordinary young woman on perpetual holiday doesn’t make for a particularly interesting heroine. Of course, peril soon surfaces to sully the endless trying-on of new frocks and posing in front of monuments. A mysterious user account for one “King Slayer,” whose profile photo is a sinister mask, begins posting graphic threats of what he’ll do to her if she doesn’t “stop talking” online. Then it becomes clear that he is tailing her in public places, uploading photos and video clips from her recent itinerary to prove it. Things soon escalate further, requiring police notification and the hiring of an ex-military security expert (Eos Karlsson).

	Yet as frightened as Chiara frequently is, and as concerned as the crew appear to be, somehow days keep going by without her ever thinking, “I gotta get the hell outta here.” When being hunted by a perp in a mask, what’s a person to do but dance at a nightclub where half the patrons are wearing glittery masks? Her follower count goes up whenever she appears scared. So even as danger rises, she visits “haunted houses” where something will inevitably get her running and screaming in dark corridors. Naturally, the climax takes place at a vast empty warehouse she and her remaining colleagues have been lured to. What could go wrong?

	It is a tribute to King and Nybroe that this increasingly implausible scenario (penned by the director and two others) doesn’t induce outright howls. Nonetheless, it is pretty silly. And the stakes aren’t very high — while likable enough, this influencer doesn’t generate any great viewer empathy. If she perishes, will the pain of diminished endorsements be felt by mid-to-upmarket fashion brands? When finally unmasked, the perp gets a big speech about the corrupting influence of influencers on impressionable minds. But you’ve certainly heard all that before, not least with considerably more weight in the current anti-social-media documentary expose “Your Attention Please.”

	One can be thankful “Project” isn’t all pseudo-“found footage,” with some of cinematographer Daniel Parmo’s images granted an omniscient POV in full widescreen. Otherwise, we get diverse formats to reflect the various media Chiara’s travails are recorded and/or posted on.
	

	A few tolerable jump scares aside, the film isn’t terribly scary, blame for which must be partly laid at the door of DJ White Shadow — who, as music supervisor and (with MFR) composer, lessens suspense with too many dance tracks, then with pedestrian thriller backing. There’s a cut duly sung by King under the closing credits entitled “Bubble Gum,” perhaps an unfortunate choice for a movie that ultimately feels no more substantial than that. Nevertheless, an obligatory post-credits tag sequence raises the specter of sequels that few are likely to clamor for.

schema.headline: ‘The Influencer Project’ Review: Found Footage Terror Takes a Tepid Danish Holiday

title: Samantha Josephs’ Debut Horror Novel ‘Carrying’ to Receive Feature Adaptation From Tommy Dorfman’s Good Girl Productions (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Samantha Josephs’ upcoming debut horror novel “Carrying,” about a transgender woman living in secret who miraculously discovers she’s pregnant, is g
body:
Samantha Josephs’ upcoming debut horror novel “Carrying,” about a transgender woman living in secret who miraculously discovers she’s pregnant, is getting a feature adaptation from Tommy Dorfman‘s Good Girl Productions. 

	Dorfman is set to direct and produce the project while Josephs will pen the screenplay. 

	An official logline for “Carrying” reads, “Martha is trans, so stealth even her family has no idea. She carved the woman she is out of the marble of a boy, and she’ll do whatever it takes to protect what she’s built. When a mysterious chronic illness and its debilitating symptoms threaten to upend her existence, she starts experimental treatments and gives in to her surprising, unsettling cravings. She’s even more shocked to discover that she’s undeniably, impossibly pregnant.” 
	

	From Putnam/Penguin Random House, “Carrying” is set to hit shelves on Oct. 6. The book was recently shortlisted for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. 


	Josephs is a New York native now living in Los Angeles. She graduated from USC’s Writing for the Screen and Television program and worked across podcasts, video games, apps and erotica before penning “Carrying.” 

	“From our very first meeting, it wasn’t just Tommy’s love for ‘Carrying’ that got me, but that she completely understood it,” Josephs said. “For a book that I know is extremely out there, it feels especially touching that she sees it and Martha so completely. As we’ve started working together, Tommy’s vision for my twisted tale has me absolutely giddy for everyone to experience. I know my baby is safe in Tommy’s capable hands.”
	

	Actress and filmmaker Dorfman launched Good Girl Productions in 2025 with a focus on developing projects for film, television and theater. Other projects on the Good Girl slate include a feature adaptation of Torrey Peters’ bestseller “Detransition, Baby,” and a movie based on Allie Rowbottom’s thriller novel “Aestetica.”

	Dorfman previously directed the coming-of-age drama “I Wish You All the Best” for Lionsgate. In front of the camera, she’s best known for her roles in “13 Reasons Why” and “Jane the Virgin.”

	Josephs is repped by UTA. Dorfman is repped by Linden Entertainment, Yorn Levi and ID PR.

schema.headline: Samantha Josephs’ Debut Horror Novel ‘Carrying’ to Receive Feature Adaptation From Tommy Dorfman’s Good Girl Productions (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Salma Hayek Pinault, Pamela Abdy, Adria Arjona, Gemma Chan and Beth de Araújo Set for WIF Honors
description:
Pamela Abdy, Adria Arjona, Beth de Araújo, Gemma Chan and Salma Hayek Pinault will be saluted at this year’s WIF Honors ceremony.

	The gala, which
body:
Pamela Abdy, Adria Arjona, Beth de Araújo, Gemma Chan and Salma Hayek Pinault will be saluted at this year’s WIF Honors ceremony.

	The gala, which directly funds the organization’s advocacy, research and career programs, will be held on Thursday, Nov. 5, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills. 

	Abdy, co-chair and CEO of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, will receive WIF’s inaugural Vanguard Award. The prize recognizes the breadth of Abdy’s career, with a particular acknowledgment of her tenure at the studio, where she has overseen blockbusters and award darlings including “One Battle After Another,” “Sinners,” “Barbie,” “Weapons,” and “Dune: Part Two.” Last year, Warner Bros. tied the all-time studio record with 11 Academy Awards from an industry-leading 30 nominations.
	

	Abdy will be presented the award by Nancy Meyers, after the studio backed Meyers’ first film in more than a decade. The comedy, starring Penélope Cruz, Kieran Culkin, Jude Law, Emma Mackey and Owen Wilson, is currently in production and slated for release on Christmas Day 2027.


	The Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film will go to filmmaker de Araújo and Chan (in absentia) for their collaboration on “Josephine,”  a harrowing drama about a young girl who accidentally witnesses a devastating crime in Golden Gate Park. The film won both the U.S. Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at Sundance and is set for limited theatrical release on Nov. 20, before expanding nationwide on December 4. The prize marks a full-circle moment for the pair: de Araújo participated in WIF’s financing intensive in 2018, while Chan was named the WIF Max Mara Face of the Future honoree in 2020. 
	

	This year’s Face of the Future prize, which recognizes a rising star, goes to Arjona. The actress in on a hot streak following her standout performance in the Peabody-winning series “Andor,” and as executive producer and star of “Los Frikis” and “Splitsville.” Arjona most recently led the A24 action thriller “Onslaught” and will next star opposite Michael B. Jordan in his reimagined “The Thomas Crown Affair” for Amazon MGM. 

	Finally, Jane Fonda will present the Humanitarian Award — named for Fonda, its inaugural recipient — to Academy Award nominee and Emmy winner Hayek Pinault. Fonda and WIF selected Hayek Pinault for the award to salute her historic career across both film and television, and for her advocacy for the rights of women, children and immigrants.

	“The 2026 honorees exemplify what WIF stands for: visionary work, fierce community, and lifting up the next generation,” said WIF CEO Kirsten Schaffer in a statement. “At a time when our Reframe research reveals a sobering backslide for women and nonbinary people in this industry, it is vital to celebrate leaders committed to transformation. Pamela Abdy, Beth de Araújo, Adria Arjona, Gemma Chan, and Salma Hayek bring indelible stories to the screen, while actively building a more inclusive culture.”

	Victoria Alonso and Andrea Nelson Meigs, co-chairs of this year’s WIF Honors, concurred. “We are proud of this slate of honorees, especially Pam Abdy, whose fearless advocacy for storytellers has helped shape the films that define our industry,” they said. “We’re equally proud to honor Adria, Salma, Gemma, and Beth, women of color in an industry where they remain underrepresented both on and off screen. All of these women deserve recognition, and we can’t wait to celebrate them this November.” 

	In addition to Alonso and Nelson Meigs, the committee also includes Syrinthia Studer, president of WIF’s board of directors, and board members Tara Duncan, Ivette Rodriguez, Rachel Rusch and Jurnee Smollett.

schema.headline: Salma Hayek Pinault, Pamela Abdy, Adria Arjona, Gemma Chan and Beth de Araújo Set for WIF Honors

title: Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards
description:
Films fronted by Jackie Chan and Anil Kapoor are among the 335 national winners named by the Asian Academy Creative Awards. 

	“The Shadow’s Edge” w
body:
Films fronted by Jackie Chan and Anil Kapoor are among the 335 national winners named by the Asian Academy Creative Awards. 

	“The Shadow’s Edge” won Best Feature Film for Chinese Mainland, and “Subedaar” won it for India.

	The winners come from 18 nations and territories and span 39 categories. They now move on to the international round. Grand winners will be named at the gala awards final at Singapore’s Capitol Theatre in December.
	

	Mediacorp led the company count with 23 wins. Prime Video India and Astro Malaysia collected 19 each, and CNN took 15.


	Chinese drama series “The Lead” won more categories than any other title, with six. They included Best Actress in a Leading Role for Liu Haocun. Best Drama Series, however, went to the bigger-budget “Legend of the Magnate.”

	Malaysia’s haul came with a note of loss. Horror feature “Malam Terlarang” (Forbidden Night) won four categories, among them Best Feature Film and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Sofia Jane. Its Best Direction (Feature Film) win went to Norhanisham bin Muhammad, who died in May. Astro’s family crime drama “Good Boys Go to Heaven” added five Malaysian wins, taking both Best Actor and the drama series prize.

	In Japan, “Song of the Samurai” also won five categories but lost Best Drama Series to “Alice in Borderland.” Non took Best Actress for “Miss King.”

	China’s “Swords Into Plowshares” also collected four wins, as did Season 3 of India’s “The Family Man.” Bai Yu was named Best Actor in a Leading Role for Chinese Mainland.

	Taiwan broadcaster PTS also scored four wins with “Dogman.” The series took Best Drama Series as well as acting honors for Chang Hsiao Chuan and Tarcy Su.
	

	GMMTV’s “Enigma Black Stage” picked up four Thai wins. Scripted categories were hotly contested. Gemini Norawit Titicharoenrak was named Best Actor for “Ticket to Heaven,” while Mono’s Manatsanun Phanlerdwongsakul took Best Actress for “Sweet Dreams.”

	In the Philippines, Vice Ganda, one of the country’s biggest stars, had to get through an extra tie-breaker round before securing Best Actor for his performance in “Call Me Mother.” Nadine Lustre, who stars opposite him in that film, also advances, though her nod is for headlining Viu’s “Love, Siargao.”

	Animated feature “The Violinist” took Best Feature Film, Best Animation and Best Screenplay for Singapore. Its voice cast includes Tan Kheng Hua and Ayden Sng. Sng was separately named Best Actor in a Leading Role (Singapore) for the series “Double Helix.” Singaporean independent Refinery Media won three categories for lifestyle show “Man of the Hour.”

	CNN’s 15 wins came in the factual categories. One went to Kristie Lu Stout, a previous winner, for Best Factual Presenter (Thailand). She will go up against another past winner, Singapore’s Wei Du, who was recognized for CNA’s “Walk the Line: ICE Nation.”

	Awards chair Beverley McGarvey, president and streaming lead at Paramount ANZ, said the awards show every year how deep the region’s pool of talent and original ideas runs. “Our stories are becoming more confident, more distinctive and more influential, not only in their home markets but with audiences all around the world,” she said. McGarvey said that entry numbers were level with last year’s. She added that the size of the national winners field makes it the world’s biggest showcase of Asia-Pacific content. This year’s jurors came from 38 countries.

	The awards use a two-round system. A jury of senior industry figures from TV networks, streamers, production outfits, distributors, buyers and screen agencies first scores entries at the national level. It scores them again in the international round to choose the grand winners.

schema.headline: Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards

title: UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit
description: UTA has taken a dramatic step to streamline the leadership of its film and TV lit and talent departments to reflect the industry trends of blurring
body:
UTA has taken a dramatic step to streamline the leadership of its film and TV lit and talent departments to reflect the industry trends of blurring lines between disciplines. As part of the change, agency veteran Matt Rice has been promoted to president of the new UTA Filmed Entertainment unit.

	In the new structure, UTA’s Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan have been elevated to  managing partners of Filmed Entertainment. UTA has named new department heads to lead key segments:  Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner will lead Motion Picture Literary; Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman will run TV Literary while talent will be steered by Hanley Baxter and John Sacks alongside longstanding talent chief Mike Jelline.
	

	Another new wrinkle is the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board that includes agency stalwarts including Jelline, Berman, Moorhead, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig and Larry Salz.


	UTA chief executive David Kramer outlined the reasoning for the changes in a memo sent to agency staffers on Thursday morning 

	“UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next,” Kramer said. “As the business evolves and film and television increasingly converge, this team positions us to lead that evolution, unlock new possibilities for our clients and bring the full power of UTA to everyone we represent.”

	Rice joined UTA in 2002 after getting his start at the Broder Kurland literary agency. He’s one of the town’s top representatives of writers, directors and showrunners, including such notables as Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Michael Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, Will Forte, Justin Halpern & Patrick Schumacker, R. Scott Gemmill, James Gunn, Dan Goor, Chris McKenna & Erik Sommers, Adam Reed, Sebastian Maniscalco and Matt Rife.
	

	“This move reflects what sets UTA apart — a bold, collaborative and forward-thinking approach. I’m excited to build upon the work of this exceptional group of leaders and continue to deliver best-in-class representation to our clients,” Rice said.

	UTA’s shakeup of its longstanding departmental lines reflects the shifting sands for the content business as well as the business of representing boldface name talent. The growth in audience and influence among the largest social media platforms has revved up the creator economy and birthed a new breed of digital media superstar. All of this has challenged the traditional operations of Hollywood’s largest talent and management firms. 

	Here is Kramer’s full memo:

	UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration.

	I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment. Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment.

	To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge.

	To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz.
	

	All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson andJordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses.

	We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success.

	Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year.

	David

	(Pictured: UTA’s Matt Rice)

schema.headline: UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit

title: Atlas Entertainment and Culture Genesis Strike Creator Content Development Pact for TV, Film and Short Form
description: Charles Roven’s Atlas Entertainment has struck a development deal with Culture Genesis, a leading-edge representation firm that packages the content
body:
Charles Roven’s Atlas Entertainment has struck a development deal with Culture Genesis, a leading-edge representation firm that packages the content of creator economy stars for sale at scale to mainstream buyers.

	The deal reflects crosscurrents in media and advertising, where all the heat is on social media creators and marketers’ demand for social video.

	The pact calls for Atlas and Culture Genesis to jointly develop film, TV and short form titles drawn from Culture Genesis’ archive of talent and content. The company operates the CG Collective, billed as 190 of YouTube’s top creators including iShowSpeed, Kai Cenat, REACT, AMP, People vs Food and V10’s America’s Funniest Home Videos. Atlas will work with Culture Genesis to develop and package new properties from its archive in addition to other projects.
	

	Roven is one of the industry’s most respected film producers, responsible for some of the biggest films of the past few decades, including “Oppenheimer,” “The Dark Knight,” “The Dark Knight Rises,” “Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice” and “Wonder Woman.” Culture Genesis represents the superstars of Gen Z including sports influencer IShowSpeed whose feed has been described as “ESPN for Gen Z.”


	“Great film and television has always been driven by the best and brightest filmmakers and storytellers,” said Roven. “Today’s creators are visionaries in their own right and audiences have clearly taken notice. We’re excited to collaborate with Culture Genesis to redefine the path from digital to film and television and introduce audiences to the next generation of talent.”
	



	

	



	Culture Genesis has grown rapidly as an exemplar of attention-economy representation firms that are reaping the rewards of social media and also forging new pathways for the most promising creators. Launched in 2018, the Santa Monica-based company is led by founder and CEO Shaun Newsum and Fred Coates, who is president.

	“Culture isn’t a demographic to target. It’s where attention is born — and creators are its authors,” said Newsum, founder & CEO of Culture Genesis. “The most valuable attention in media now lives with creators, not channels. Through our collaboration with Atlas, we’re giving creators exposure to potential economics that have historically been closed to digital-native talent.”

	Coates pointed out that traditional Hollywood and creators have more in common that it would seem on the surface.

	“Atlas saw what Culture Genesis built — a collective of 190 creators with broadcast-scale, independently measured audiences — and understood immediately that this is infrastructure, not inventory,” Coates said. “We’re bringing two proven engines together: their ability to develop and sell world-class film and television, and our ability to reach an audience that already shows up. That’s real upside on both sides of the table.”

	Culture Genesis says its portfolio reaches more than 43 million U.S. households each month with 9.5 billion monthly impressions and 60% of viewing on the living-room screen.

	Atlas Entertainment is headed by Roven and producing partner Alex Gartner. The firm’s upcoming projects include Michael B. Jordan’s redo of “The Thomas Crown Affair” for Amazon MGM Studios and “Road House 2” for Amazon Prime Video. It’s also finishing up production on the Imax documentary “Frontier,” about the work of photographer Anouk Masson Krantz.

	(Pictured: Atlas Entertainment’s Charles Roven, Culture Genesis’ Shaun Newsum)

title: Searchlight Submits Original Song From ‘Behemoth!’ for Oscars, ‘Your God Is Sleeping’ Written by Lukas Frank (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Searchlight Pictures will officially submit “Your God Is Sleeping” from “Behemoth!,” a new drama film by Tony Gilroy, for consideration in the origi
body:
Searchlight Pictures will officially submit “Your God Is Sleeping” from “Behemoth!,” a new drama film by Tony Gilroy, for consideration in the original song category at the Oscars, Variety has learned exclusively.

	The film stars Pedro Pascal as Alex Serian, a gifted musician and cellist who returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. 

	“Your God Is Sleeping” is written by singer and songwriter Lukas Frank who is also one of the film’s nine composers known as the Behemoth! Collective.
	

	Speaking about the song, Frank told Variety, “Tony told me he needed a song for a superhuman child prodigy—‘like Björk meets Beethoven … except cooler.’ Something like that … very easy, right? I ended up just trying to channel the music I loved when I was a young music nerd, building the song around the title, which was in Tony’s script.”

	Gilroy, who wrote and directed the film, which will premiere this Friday at the New York Film Festival, told Variety he had known Frank for almost a decade. “My correspondence with Lukas goes back to 2018, when he started sending me his early demos, and I was really into him because he was a studio drummer,” Gilroy said. He added, “I’ve had a ringside seat for the evolution of Storefront Church (Frank’s band) and became a really big believer in it and what he’s doing. Lukas’ music always just grabs me — it’s so unique.”

	When it came to writing the song, Gilroy offered Frank a chance to take a shot at it. “He just killed it,” Gilroy said of the final song.

	He also noted that while there’s a version of the song that appears in the film, another special mix is being put together for the film’s soundtrack. “There’s the version of ‘Your God Is Sleeping,’ which is in the film, mixed in a certain way. But then we did another mix for it for the soundtrack version — we did a radio mix. They brought in (producer) Dave Sardy and just pumped it, and man, it really pops.”
	

	“Behemoth!” will be released in theaters on Dec. 4.

title: Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute
description: He’s a “great guy who’s incredibly humble” who has also produced 38 movies in 17 years that have delivered more than $35 billion at the box office.
body:
He’s a “great guy who’s incredibly humble” who has also produced 38 movies in 17 years that have delivered more than $35 billion at the box office. Twelve of those titles delivered more than $1 billion; three of them generated $2 billion apiece. Not to mention, Kevin Feige is the architect of the most meticulously crafted, interconnected cinematic universe in the history of motion pictures.

	Disney Entertainment chairman Alan Bergman reeled off those stunning stats (and admirable qualities) as he took part in Wednesday night’s tribute to Feige, president of Marvel Studios and chief creative officer of Marvel, who was honored with this year’s Pioneer of the Year laurel from the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation. 
	

	“Guardians of the Galaxy” star Chris Pratt and writer-director Jon Favreau were on hand at the Beverly Hilton hotel to laud the Marvel leader. Composer Michael Giacchino was there via video because of illness. Others who paid tribute in prerecorded reels include Marvel’s Louis D’Esposito and MCU stars Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell, Chris Hemsworth, Paul Bettany, Hailee Steinfeld, Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby.


	Feige was the star of the night but the conversation in the packed ballroom was dominated by the big news of the day, Paramount Skydance’s surprise news that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz is leaving the toymaker to join the Melrose plant as co-CEO with David Ellison.

	“He believes in the movies, and even more than that he believes in the people who make the movies,” Pratt told the crowd at the Beverly Hilton. The event raised $1.9 million for the Will Rogers Pioneers Assistance Fund, which helps those in the film exhibition community who need assistance. Also in the crowd were Disney chief Josh D’Amaro, AMC Theatres leader Adam Aron and Eduardo Acuna of Regal Cinemas, producer Scott Stuber among others. 
	

	Favreau echoed Pratt’s comments about Feige’s passion for all things related to cinema.

	“The man loves movies. He listens to movie soundtracks in his car,” the “Iron Man” director told the crowd. “He’s driving down PCH blasting the ‘Ferngully’ soundtrack.”

	Feige took a bit of gentle ribbing about his love of custom baseball caps and other characteristics that have become his signature. From video, Giacchino introduced a large tiki band that emerged on stage to perform Marvel movie tunes with a Polynesian flair. 

	The executive and producer lived up to his advance billing for humility in his remarks at the end of the night. And he had some thoughtful observations about what it is that makes moviegoing so special. He even name-checked his childhood haunt, the Rialto Theater in Westfield, New Jersey. (“Sitting in the dark, eating Twizzlers. I was hooked,” he recalled.)

	“Underneath all the technology and the spectacle, the years of work from development to post. It’s still the same thing: a group of people making something with others, and then a group of people sitting in the dark and experiencing it with others. That is the full process of a movie,” Feige said. 

	“The final crucial part of that collaboration is the audience. Movies are an invitation to experience a story together. When a film connects and the crowd is cheering, laughing and crying together, that shared emotion is the final step in the process. That’s the real movie magic, You might even say it’s not a real movie without it,” he said.

schema.headline: Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute

title: Larry Nassar Removed from Michigan Sex Offender List
description:
Larry Nassar
                          Removed From Michigan Sex Offender Registry
body:
Larry Nassar
                          Removed From Michigan Sex Offender Registry
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 1, 2026
                            10:03 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Michigan just wiped 20,000 convicted sex offenders off its sex offender registry ... and Larry Nassar was one of them.
      
    
            Here's what happened ... Michigan's Supreme Court recently ruled that amendments issued in 2021 to the Sex Offender Registration Act can't be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents ... and as a result, the Michigan State Police scrubbed 20K sex offenders whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            That means Nassar's been scrubbed from the registry ... and a search for his name yields no results.
      

            The Eaton County prosecutor's office wrote on social media ... "The Michigan Supreme Court’s decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning."
      
    
            As you know, Nassar was the team doctor for the U.S. women's gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014 and the team physician at Michigan State University until 2016 ... where he used his position to sexually assault hundreds of athletes.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to CBS News, the prosecutor's office said ... "His conduct occurred before 2011 despite his convictions coming after."
      
    
            The Prosecuting Attorney's Office wrote on social media that the court had another choice that would have allowed offenders to remain registered, but says the court decided to "toss the scalpel aside and use a chainsaw."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Nassar's currently serving multiple lengthy prison sentences that will last for decades ... but the ruling is still pretty alarming, considering tens of thousands of offenders will no longer show up in the registry.
